description: Golden Dataset for Objective 2 (thesis paper, Section 3.2.1). Forty standardized academic queries spanning the CCSICT academic catalog -- the Data Mining, Web and Mobile Application Development, and Network and Security specializations, and the BSDSA, BSIS and BLIS programs, which carry no specialization and are therefore identified by program code (services/catalog.py::resolve_academic_selection) -- plus cross-track and negative-control items. Every ground_truth answer must be derived directly from the archived CCSICT thesis corpus and validated by a panel of three CCSICT faculty members before serving as the absolute mathematical benchmark for the Ragas evaluation. The corpus CCSICT released on 2026-09-07 holds twelve manuscripts covering BSCS Data Mining, BSIS and BLIS only, so every query also carries corpus_coverage, which records whether the released corpus can support an answer at all: absent_by_design (the 3 negative controls, absent by construction), absent_unreleased (5 queries whose own text is scoped to a program or specialization the department did not release) and undetermined (the remaining 32). undetermined is the honest default, not a placeholder to be filled in mechanically: most questions ask about CCSICT theses generally rather than about one track, so whether a released manuscript answers them is a judgement about content that only the panel drafting the ground truth can make. It must never be inferred from the category label, which records which part of the catalog a query was written to probe, not which manuscripts exist. validate_formal_dataset refuses a formal run while any query is still undetermined. Accuracy is interpreted on the present stratum and refusal behaviour on the absent strata; run_comparison.py reports Answer Correctness both pooled and split this way.

workflow: 1. Ingest the released twelve-thesis corpus into the system.
2. For each query, the researchers draft a ground_truth answer strictly from the archived manuscripts and record the exact source thesis (title, authors, year).

3. Set corpus_coverage from what step 2 found, never from the category label: present when a released manuscript answers the query, absent_unreleased when it cannot because the department released no thesis from the program or specialization the query is about, absent_by_design for the negative controls. The five queries already marked absent_unreleased are scoped to an unreleased track by their own wording; confirm them rather than re-derive them.

4. For either absent stratum the ground_truth states the absence explicitly and source_thesis is 'none'. Say which absence it is: no manuscript from that program was released, or the released manuscripts do not cover the topic. Those are different findings, and preserving the distinction is why the stratum exists.
5. Each of the three faculty panel members reviews every ground_truth and its assigned stratum against the corpus and signs off below.
6. Set validated_by_faculty_panel to true only after all three sign-offs. run_comparison.py warns until then, and refuses a formal run while any query is undetermined.

instrument_revisions.change: Query categories relabelled to the ISU Echague academic catalog. Ids 29 and 33 additionally had their QUESTION TEXT reworded: both named a retired track grouping (Intelligent Systems, Information Management) that services/catalog.py::AMBIGUOUS_LEGACY_TRACKS retires and the catalog never defined, so they asked about a category the system has no concept of. They now name the BSDSA and BSIS programs respectively.
instrument_revisions.rationale: Recorded here, not only in version control, because a reworded question changes what the instrument asks. Panel members drafting ground_truth answers must be able to see that these two differ from the pre-2026-08-25 dataset. No ground_truth had been drafted at the time of the change; all forty were still REPLACE placeholders, so no validated work was invalidated.

instrument_revisions.change: No question text changed. Every query gained corpus_coverage and coverage_basis after CCSICT released the actual corpus: twelve distinct undergraduate manuscripts, five BSCS Data Mining (2024), three BSIS (2025) and four BLIS (2026). A fourteenth staged PDF, the k-means manuscript, came from its author rather than the release and the thesis adviser declined it as an addition on 2026-09-07, so the corpus is the twelve released manuscripts. The department selected and released these itself and provided no BSIT (Web and Mobile Application Development, Network and Security) or BSDSA manuscripts.
instrument_revisions.rationale: The stratum was first assigned from each query category, which was wrong in both directions and was caught in review before any ground truth had been drafted. Category records which part of the catalog a query probes, not which manuscripts exist, and most of these questions ask about CCSICT theses generally: query 6 asks about recommender systems, which the released Mango Fruit Quality thesis builds, yet its BSDSA category had marked it unanswerable; query 1 asks which theses applied Retrieval-Augmented Generation, which none of the twelve do, yet its Data Mining category had marked it answerable. Either error inverts the interpretation the study commits to, because a correct grounded answer would be scored against a ground truth asserting absence, or a correct refusal against one asserting an answer exists. Only two determinations survive without reading the corpus: a negative control is absent by construction, and a query whose own wording is scoped to an unreleased program or specialization cannot be answered whatever the manuscripts contain. The other thirty-two are undetermined until the panel drafts their ground truth, and the harness refuses a formal run until every one is resolved.
